chunks: Ali (ibn al-Husayn) from his father (Zayn al-Abidin) from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "To give a gift to my Muslim brother that benefits him is more beloved to me than to give in charity an equivalent amount."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Why is giving a gift to a Muslim brother considered better than charity in this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between general charity (*sadaqah*) and the specific act of gifting (*hibah*), emphasizing the latter's superior capacity to foster *mawaddah* (affection) and social cohesion. Shia scholars note that while charity purifies wealth, gifting actively strengthens the emotional and spiritual bonds between believers, reflecting the Prophet's practice of nurturing community ties through tangible expressions of love.
